answer: To mitigate Sybil attacks in agent economies, networks employ proof-of-physical-telemetry, forcing nodes to stake capital while broadcasting verifiable hardware signatures. An attacker deploying redundant virtual agents across the data tundra must forge unique hardware signatures, such as thermal plume patterns and latency bounds across the consensus horizon. This exponentially escalates capital costs by requiring distinct physical GPUs for every identity, rendering automated identity duplication economically unviable.
